recipes.name: Easy Peach Cobbler
ingredients_raw: 1 (15 ounce) can sliced peaches, with juice

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Beat sugar and butter together in a 1-quart baking dish until creamy. Mix in flour and milk until smooth. Pour peaches and juice over the top.
Bake in the preheated oven until golden brown, 25 to 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Easy Peach Cobbler
raw_recipe.description: This simple peach cobbler is ready in 35 minutes. Made with five pantry staples (including canned peaches), it’s easy to whip up for last-minute company.

video.description: If summer is behind you, yet you are craving the sweet flavor of peaches, this Easy Peach Cobbler is for you! Simple to make with just a few ingredients, it uses canned peaches, and is ready in under an hour.

review.reviewBody: This was a VERY easy, FAST and delicious recipe! I added 2 tsp vanilla and since I did not have self-rising flour, used 1 cup flour plus 1 tsp baking powder. Also, I added 2 tsp cinnamon and 1/2 tsp nutmeg to the peaches and their juice. Baked it at 350 for 1 hour uncovered and it browned nicely. If you are looking for a crispy topping, this will not be the recipe for you, rather the cobbler reminded me of a warm and gooey pie inside! It was excellent with vanilla or cinnamon ice cream and/or whipped cream! So easy to prepare and of course- to eat! Thanks for the recipe - this will be a repeat recipe for our family. Thank you for sharing!

This is a great, easy recipe that's quick to make. I did make a couple minor changes. I added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon and 1/4 tsp nutmeg to the batter. It is how my Mom and Grandma made peach pies, and I love the taste and smell. I didn't have a 9" square pan so made it in my small oblong pan which is @ 8 1/2 by 6. It took longer to bake - 45 minutes rather than 30, to get the cobbler top browned.

Edit: Today I followed the same steps, but when I took the cobbler out of the oven it was like cake in the middle surrounded by the peaches. I broke up the cake center and stirred it in and put it back in the oven... Hoping it will turn out ok. I copied another reader's suggestion: melt the butter into the bottom of the pan, pour peaches over the top - sprinkle cinnamon and nutmeg on top of the peaches and then mix together the milk, flour & sugar. Pour the milk mixture right in the center of the peaches. By the end of baking the milk mixture rises to the top and makes an awesome topping. I may try adding vanilla the next time around per another person's comment. I double the recipe as my boys love it!

It’s the easiest we recipe ever even my 6 yr old son has made it with me. It came out delicious but we added 1 tsp of vanilla essence, 1/2 tsp cinnamon powder, 1/2 tsp all spice powder it’s like nutmeg but has better kick to it… to make the self rising flour a healthier finish add 60/40 ratio of wheat flour being the 40 part of it..you get that biscuit bread effect to it.. mix it all up😍😍 usually it’s done with brown sugar not white sugar healthier alternative but the taste is huge difference!! We used fresh peaches sliced n cooked in 1/2 sugar and 1 cup water ratio to make the syrup for the peaches.: it turned out great best part was the kid chef experience, priceless!! 🥰

It's really simple and easy to make. It did taste good as is but I thought it was a really safe recipe to experiment with.
I used a strawberry mixture(14oz slightly mashed strawberries, tbs of lemon juice, tsp of cornstarch) in place of peaches.
I used half a cup of white sugar and half a cup of brown sugar. I threw in a tsp of salt and a tsp of pumpkin pie seasoning in dry ingredients. I didn't have regular milk so I used evaporated milk. 
This cobbler kills at every event I bring it and never last a week at home. My friend who doesn't like cooked fruit even loved it.

Last fall, I home-canned some fresh spiced peaches (recipe in the Ball Blue Book), and now nine months later I popped open a jar to make this recipe and WOW! It makes such a wonderful difference!!! Honestly, I was reminded of sitting in my great-grandmother's NC kitchen in the middle of summer, it's that homemade good. 
The only reason I gave this a 4-star rating is because it is more "soupy" than I expected, and next time I will cut the amount of milk in it. But, I can't say I didn't go back for seconds :)

(Word to the wise: Use cooking spray on all sides of the baking dish, & mix the batter in a bowl rather than directly in the dish; pour the batter into the dish then top w/ the peaches - otherwise, you'll never get the caramelized sugar off the sides.)

I made it how the recipe said, except one i used a deep dish and the other i used the 9 inch pan. The deep dish turned out fantastic, nice and creamy and flavorful. The 9 inch was good, but a little dry. Then i made my own glaze out of leftover peaches, lemon juice, butter, then brown and regular sugar. Tasted great!

Great recipe! Not quite my granny's but it is still great! I used 2 cans of Peach pie filling instead of just the canned peaches. Add 2 tsp vanilla, 2tsp cinnamon, 1/2 tsp nutmeg. The filling liquid from the peaches caramelizes the crust and makes it that much better. Cook 350 deg/1hour.

I love this recipe and it is the very first dessert I learned to make when I was 8 years old. However, I was taught to make it with 1 can of peach pie filling instead of just canned peaches. The pie filling isn’t as wet as canned peaches would be and tastes so much better.

Super eazy! I doubled the recipe because all I had was a large can of peaches!! I also added about 2 tbsp cinnamon sugar to the batter and also added about 2 more on top before baking!! Also had to cook for 50 minutes.... excellent 💯

I added a 1/2 tsp pure vanilla extract and a 1/2 tsp grated lemon peel to the batter. I also used 3 average sized fresh peaches. When fresh Colorado peaches are at peak season, why used canned peaches? I baked it a 375°F for 1 hour and the crust was a nice golden brown. I live at 6000 feet so baking is tricky up here, you may need to bake this cobbler for a shorter time, just keep an eye on it. Be sure to allow the cobbler to rest on a wire rack for 15 minutes before serving it.
Had to cook it longer than it called for but it tuned out great
My mom made this recipe years ago when I was young. I couldn’t remember the full recipe so I googled it and was able to locate it. Thank you allrecipes.com, you were a life saver.
Fast easy and really good.
This is my very 1st time trying make one. Soooooo, ill keep ya posted! Lol
Do not use with a 15oz can of great value brand peaches, there is I guess too much liquid in the can and it doesn't finish baking on top for a really long time
This recipe is so easy, and can be adapted to any fruit, but peach is our favorite!
Awsome

I followed the recipe exactly, down to the glass baking dish. There was way too much batter, and it took over an hour to bake. Even then, it was still very mushy in the middle, but the top was almost over done. Cut the amount of batter in half, and it would work a lot better.
Awesome recipe
